chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' from Salih ibn Uqbah from Abdullah ibn Muhammad who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in Mina, and I wanted to ask him about a matter. He said, so I began to feel shy of him. He said to me, 'O Abdullah, ask.' I said, 'May I be your ransom, I bought a slave girl,' then I remained silent out of shyness towards him. He said to me, 'I think you wanted to have intercourse with her, but you did not know how to do so.' I said, 'Yes, may I be your ransom.' He said, 'And I think you wanted to perform istibra' for her, and you were shy to ask about it.' I said, 'Indeed, your shyness prevented me from that.' He said, 'There is no harm in performing istibra' for her, and if you wait, it is better for you.'

A man said to him, 'May I be your ransom, I have heard more than one person say that istibra' is permissible.' I said to him, 'And what is the preference in leaving it?' He said, 'Like that; if there was harm in it, we would not have commanded it.'

He said, then he turned to me and said, 'A man comes to his slave girl, she clings to him, and he sees blood while she is pregnant, so he thinks that is menstruation, so he sells her. And I do not like for the Muslim man to have intercourse with the slave girl who has become pregnant by another man until he comes to him and informs him.'

key_terms.التَّفْخِيذ: Istibra': The waiting period for a female slave to confirm she is not pregnant before her new owner has intercourse with her.
key_terms.تَسْتَبْرِئَهَا: To perform istibra' for her / to verify her pregnancy status.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on istibra' for a purchased slave girl and how to confirm paternity?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) psychological insight, as he intuitively discerned the companion’s hesitation regarding *istibra'* (the waiting period to confirm lineage) and the act of *tafkhidh* (inducing menstruation). It underscores the Shia juristic principle that while *istibra'* is recommended to ensure the child's lineage (*luhooq*) is correctly attributed to the owner, it is not strictly obligatory, reflecting a balance between legal certainty and ease. The narration also clarifies the specific scenario where a slave girl pregnant by a previous owner is sold, warning the new owner against assuming the current pregnancy is from him to avoid lineage confusion.
